name: PET Surface Ester Depolymerization (PETase primary cleavage)
description: Endo- and exo-type cleavage of ester linkages in accessible amorphous segments of Poly(ethylene terephthalate) by PET-hydrolyzing esterases.

reaction_steps.name: Enzyme Adsorption & Ester Docking
reaction_steps.mechanism: PETase hydrophobic cleft interacts with the aromatic ring of the polymer chain, aligning the ester carbonyl carbon with the Ser160 nucleophile.

reaction_steps.name: Ester Bond Hydrolysis & Primary Intermediate Release
reaction_steps.mechanism: Nucleophilic attack followed by water-mediated hydrolysis yielding soluble mono-(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (MHET) as major product, alongside minor bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) and free terephthalic acid (TPA).

products.name: Mono-(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (MHET)
products.biological_impact: Feedback inhibitor of PETase catalytic turnover at elevated concentrations.

products.name: Bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET)
products.biological_impact: Trace intermediate from dual end-chain cleavage.

products.name: Terephthalic Acid (TPA)
products.solubility: Low water solubility at acidic pH; ionizes to terephthalate at pH >5
products.biological_impact: Direct precursor for repolymerization; causes progressive medium acidification.

environmental_implications.carbon_fate: Conversion of persistent macromolecular polymer into water-soluble aromatic monomers.
environmental_implications.toxicity_profile: Non-toxic biodegradable intermediate metabolites; MHET and TPA are non-bioaccumulative under aerobic composting.
environmental_implications.ph_impact: Continuous release of carboxylic acid protons (pKa1 ~3.5, pKa2 ~4.46) reduces medium pH if unbuffered, leading to self-limiting enzyme denaturation.

name: MHET Secondary Hydrolysis (MHETase cleavage)
description: Specific hydrolysis of mono-(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate into monomeric terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG).

reaction_steps.name: MHET Coordination in Catalytic Pocket
reaction_steps.mechanism: Lid domain coordinates the benzoic acid moiety of MHET while the ester bond is positioned adjacent to Ser225.

products.name: Terephthalic Acid (TPA)
products.solubility: Insoluble acid; soluble as terephthalate dianion
products.biological_impact: Pure repolymerization feedstock for circular virgin-grade PET.

products.name: Ethylene Glycol (EG)
products.biological_impact: Readily assimilated by environmental microorganisms as carbon source; low aquatic toxicity at low concentrations.

environmental_implications.carbon_fate: Complete mineralizable or recyclable monomer recovery.
environmental_implications.toxicity_profile: Ethylene glycol readily biodegrades under aerobic environmental conditions (BOD5/COD > 0.6).
environmental_implications.ph_impact: Net release of 1 mol H+ per mol MHET hydrolyzed.

name: Thermophilic PET Total Depolymerization (LCC-ICCG Cutinase)
description: High-temperature direct catalytic breakdown of post-consumer PET near its glass-transition temperature (72°C) yielding monomeric TPA and EG.

reaction_steps.name: High-Mobility Thermal Depolymerization
reaction_steps.mechanism: At 72°C, polymer chain mobility at amorphous domains is elevated (Tg regime). Engineered disulfide-stabilized LCC-ICCG cuts internal and terminal ester bonds rapidly without requiring separate MHETase.

environmental_implications.carbon_fate: Rapid closed-loop bottle-to-bottle recycling without petrochemical cracking.
environmental_implications.toxicity_profile: Eliminates toxic chemical recycling solvents (e.g. glycolysis heavy metal catalysts).
environmental_implications.ph_impact: Severe rapid acidification occurs within hours; requires automated base addition (NaOH).
